meta.title: Buyer at a multi-location resort retailer
meta.industry: Resort retail, six shops across two resorts
meta.blurb: Buys apparel, gifts and sundries for the resort shops and manages vendor relationships.

opportunities.quote: I track vendor and carrier replies in a spreadsheet
opportunities.why: You spend time asking vendors and carriers for updates and tracking who has replied.
opportunities.firstStep: Move one recurring request into a form or workflow that sends reminders by itself.
opportunities.failureMode: People ignore automated reminders that arrive too often.

opportunities.why: You get a high volume of vendor and shop manager email in Outlook that you sort by hand.
opportunities.firstStep: Turn on the inbox summary each morning and copy its action items into your to-do list for a week.
opportunities.failureMode: Summaries miss the one message that mattered, so important senders still need a rule that flags them.

habits.name: Grouping similar tasks
becauseTasks: Outlook: Triage the inbox, Answer vendor questions, Chase late shipments
Excel: Check sell-through by shop, Build the weekly sales report, Reconcile vendor invoices against receipts
habits.firstStep: Put the tasks that use the same tool into one block on your calendar.
habits.failureMode: Blocks get booked over unless they are marked busy.

rules.name: Task is in the task map
Quoted evidence appears word for word in the visitor's answers
Pattern is in the catalog and every required signal was recorded
Tool is listed on the pattern, with a working link checked within the limit
Hours figures are the ones code computed
A working-habit suggestion carries no hours unless the catalog supplies a share

transcript.question: About how many emails do you go through for "Triage the inbox" each day?
transcript.answer: About 80 emails a day, mostly vendor confirmations, shipping notices and shop manager questions.

transcript.question: For "Triage the inbox", where do the emails come from, and where do they go once sorted?
options: Vendors in; sorted into Outlook folders
Mixed senders; replies sent back directly
Mixed senders; items logged in NetSuite
transcript.answer: Vendors and shop managers in; I sort them in Outlook, and answers come from the open-orders spreadsheet.

transcript.question: How many purchase orders do you write per week, and what do you base them on?
transcript.answer: I type purchase orders into NetSuite from vendor line sheets, about fifteen lines each.

transcript.question: Once a purchase order is written in NetSuite, where does it go or who receives it?
options: Sent to the vendor by email
Goes to a manager for approval

transcript.question: For "Chase late shipments", how many shipments do you chase per week, and how do you find out they're late?
options: Any count; shop managers tell me
transcript.answer: I chase late shipments two to four times a week, and I track vendor and carrier replies in a spreadsheet.

transcript.question: For "Chase late shipments", who receives your follow-ups or the updated status once you've chased?
options: Nobody, it stays in my spreadsheet
